critical_changes: Calibrate the headline agreement claims in the Abstract and Introduction. The 31-feature D > 1 verdicts reflect over-sized differences (Q > 2beta); they reverse under a single held-out rescaling (Table 15), and only two survive Bonferroni over configurations. FLUX.2 Max's aggregate D < 1 rests mainly on the Cezanne contrast, with near-zero differentiation among the Impressionists (Table 17, Fig. 4). Replace 'in CSD none does' with an interval-based statement: Nano Banana 2 has D = 0.999 with 51.3% of joint resamples below 1, and Sunburst's interval includes 1.

Report the per-family faithful and exact-differences benchmarks for the main collection (already in painter_tmlr_diagnostics_v1 hand31[*].families) in Table 7, and reinterpret or narrow the feature-family contribution. GPT Image 1's 48.6% texture fraction comes from B/H = 3.11. The mean exact-differences benchmark is itself 3.1 points lower for texture than for colour (74.7 vs 77.8%), about half the observed -6.1-point gap, and the faithful benchmark runs the other way (89.4 vs 87.2%).

Correct three factual misstatements: (a) p.1 attributes the named-minus-unnamed proximity gain to Su et al. (2025), who report named-vs-unnamed CLIP similarity and named-to-prototype similarity but no gain; (b) p.13 'whatever the model does' holds only for beta <= 1, since the painter-specific term is H*beta/4; (c) p.10 'no genuine split has an error above 0.53' uses the maximum upper end of central 95% ranges, so about 2.5% of splits exceed it by construction; the data support 'none exceeds 1'.
minor_changes: Add content-matched (class) reference targets for the CLIP and CSD agreement scores on the 11 non-mixed scenes, analogous to Table 20, to test whether the representation-dependence of D reflects subject-mix differences in r_a.

Show the across-configuration decomposition of proximity-gain differences into shared and painter-specific terms. In CLIP the shared term's variance is about 11 times the specific term's; in CSD the two terms are negatively correlated. This directly supports the Section 5.4 explanation.
Commit to releasing the generated images (reduced resolution fits the 100 MB supplement limit) and add an appendix contact sheet of all 14 scenes.
State in Section 3 that the visual content labels (230 of 870 disagreements) were AI-assigned and not verified by a human, like the crops.
Bring forward from Appendix D that the genuine-painting controls' expected value is essentially target sampling noise, because pseudo-scenes have no fixed content.
Reduce numeric density in Sections 5.3-5.4 by moving secondary values into tables.
In the Discussion, put the caveat that any painting-like movement would also raise prototype similarity next to the statement that the shared change increases similarity to the average prototype.
factual_errors: p.1 (Introduction): 'comparing with the image generated without the name turns it into a gain (Su et al., 2025)'. Su et al. Table 1(a) reports CLIP similarity between named and name-removed images and prototype similarity of named images only; it reports no named-minus-unnamed proximity gain.

p.13 (Discussion, Recommendation 2): 'a shared term larger than a quarter of the painter spread will dominate proximity whatever the model does'. False for aligned amplitude beta > 1, where the painter-specific term H*beta/4 exceeds H/4; GPT Image 2's corrected beta is 1.071 in the features.

p.10 (Section 5.3): 'In the embeddings no genuine split has an error above 0.53'. The 0.53 is the maximum of the 97.5th percentiles (build_assets.py line 1743; np.quantile in painter_tmlr_diagnostics_v3.py line 93), so about 25 of 1,000 splits in the CLIP class-sampling/pooled-target control exceed it. The output supports 'no split exceeds 1'.
